Elena Ramos: Heads-up — starting the integration plan for FlashAttention v2/v3 into the runtime kernel chooser. Posting quick perf probes + a suggested rollout. TL;DR: v3 wins on short seq (<1024) but we see regressions for paged-attn with low KV page hit rates. Planning a small canary next Tue. @Mike L @Raj Patel please review.

Mike L: Ack. can you paste the raw numbers? also which HW? A100 or H100? :eyes:

Elena Ramos: Quick numbers (A100, pytorch compile, isolated perf harness):
```
512 seq, batch=8: v2 = 68k tok/s, v3 = 83k tok/s (+22%)
1024 seq, batch=4: v2 = 42k tok/s, v3 = 51k tok/s (+21%)
2048 seq, batch=2: v2 = 21k tok/s, v3 = 19k tok/s (-9%)
paged-attn, kv_hit~30%: v3 p50 tail latency +35% vs v2, throughput -12%
fused-attn (kv warm): v3 +10% for 4096 seq on local bench
```
Notes: v3 uses more aggressive fused kernels and different memory layout which helps short-context batching but hurts when we fetch many KV pages (extra mem-copy and async IO contention).

Raj Patel: Interesting. are we running the same quantization path? any int8 changes? Also curious if the kernel selector is switching at the right seq thresholds.

Elena Ramos: Good Q. These runs were FP16. We ran a separate int8 experiment and saw similar relative wins for v3 at short seq, but int8 made the long-seq regressions worse (likely memory alignment + page fragmentation). Kernel selector currently uses a simple threshold (seq_len < 1536 -> flashv3, else flashv2). That heuristic is too coarse for paged workloads.

Zara Chen: Proposal for rollout flags / gating:
- Start canary on dedicated canary pool (10 machines, mixed user traffic)
- Feature flag: enable_flash_attention_v3 = off by default
- Canary phase 1: FF=on for 5% traffic routed to canary pool for 24h
- Phase 2: increase to 25% for 48h if no perf regressions
- Auto-fallback: route requests that have >200ms p95 regressions back to v2
- Rollback cooldown 30m
(we should codify these in infra config) :white_check_mark:

Ben Torres: We need better telemetry to detect the paged-attn regression automatically. Suggested metrics / traces:
- per-route kernel selected (v2/v3/fused)
- kv_page_hit_rate and kv_page_miss_io_ms
- per-kernel p50/p95/p99 latency by seq_len bucket (256/512/1024/2048/4096)
- sudden throughput delta alarms (>10% drop over 5m)

Mike L: We should also adjust kernel selection heuristics to consider kv_page_hit_rate + batch_size, not only seq_len. e.g.:
```python
# pseudo heuristic
if kv_page_hit_rate < 0.6 and seq_len >= 1024:
    choose = "flashv2_paged_fallback"
elif batch_size >= 8 and seq_len < 1024:
    choose = "flashv3_fused"
else:
    choose = "latency_optimized"
```
We can expose this as a server-side flag and A/B test it.

Elena Ramos: Agree. Also adding async prefetch on KV pages helped in a small experiment: page_hit_bias=0.8 + async_prefetch=true reduced p95 by ~18% on mixed workloads. Example runtime config (for the canary):
```json
{
  "kernel_selector": "latency_aware",
  "enable_flash_v3": true,
  "kv_cache_policy": "page_bias=0.8,async_prefetch=true",
  "ff_rollout_percent": 5
}
```

Raj Patel: Important to add per-model rollout pins. Some models (dense long-context ones) should be pinned to v2 until we resolve paged path. Also add unit perf tests in CI: a 4k-context end-to-end scenario that runs nightly.

Ben Torres: I'll add the alarms and dashboards. Proposed alert thresholds:
- kernel_mismatch_rate > 2% (unexpected kernel switch warnings)
- kv_page_miss_io_ms p95 > 50ms -> raise incident
- per-kernel throughput drop > 12% over 10m -> page on-call
I'll create the dashboard and share link in this thread.

Mike L: For rollback safety, we should include a lightweight deterministic fallback in the request path: add header X-Runtime-Kernel-Fallback=allow that will let the router force v2 if downstream signals show td_failures.

Elena Ramos: Action items:
- Elena: compile full perf matrix (seq x batch x kv_hit) and upload to perf bucket by EOD today
- Raj: add 4k nightly perf job + CI perf test by Friday
- Ben: dashboards + alerts for the metrics above by EOD tomorrow
- Zara: create feature flag rollout automation and canary runbook (include rollback steps)
- Mike: implement improved kernel selection heuristic as runtime flag (A/B)
- Ops: monitor canary and surface any regressions to #incidents

Elena Ramos: Thanks — will post the perf artifacts once uploaded. If folks see any anomalies in the canary, tag @Elena Ramos and escalate. :rocket:
